questions.def: Passive voice uses 'was/were + past participle' to show the subject is acted upon.
questions.question: The new research ___ by several leading scientists.

questions.def: Past perfect passive 'had been + past participle' for actions completed before a past time.
questions.question: The documents ___ before the meeting commenced.

questions.def: Future passive 'will be + past participle' indicates future action on the subject.
questions.question: The data ___ thoroughly before publication.

questions.def: 'Mistakes' is plural, requiring 'were' in the passive construction.
questions.question: Mistakes ___ made, but lessons were learned.

questions.def: 'Is suspected of' is the correct passive form with the appropriate preposition.
questions.question: The suspect ___ being watched for several weeks.

questions.def: Past passive 'was + past participle' indicates a past action on the subject.
questions.question: He ___ of the decision yesterday.

questions.def: 'Was brought' is the correct passive form of 'bring' in the past tense.
questions.question: The project ___ to a halt due to lack of funding.

questions.def: 'Will be' is required for the future passive construction.
questions.question: The regulations ___ strictly enforced from next month.

questions.def: 'Is reported' is the correct passive form for stating a general fact.
questions.question: It ___ that the company is struggling.

questions.def: 'Are being' is the present continuous passive form.
questions.question: The paintings ___ carefully restored by experts.

questions.def: 'Had been' is the past perfect passive, showing action completed earlier.
questions.question: The problem ___ already addressed in the previous report.

questions.def: 'Is being considered' describes ongoing passive action in the present.
questions.question: The proposal ___ carefully by the committee.

questions.def: 'Was' is the singular past passive form needed here.
questions.question: The error ___ discovered after a thorough investigation.

questions.def: 'Are' shows present simple passive for regularly occurring actions.
questions.question: These issues ___ regularly addressed in the forum.

questions.def: 'Are expected' is the correct passive form expressing a general expectation.
questions.question: The results ___ to be announced next week.

questions.def: 'Will be' indicates future passive form: will be held.
questions.question: The meeting ___ held in the main conference room.

questions.def: 'Must be' is the correct modal passive form.
questions.question: The information ___ kept confidential at all times.

questions.def: 'Is known' is the correct passive form for stating a general fact.
questions.question: He ___ to be one of the best researchers.

questions.def: 'Will be' is necessary for future passive construction.
questions.question: The new bridge ___ officially opened next month.

questions.def: 'Is being' shows ongoing passive action in the present.
questions.question: The decision ___ appealed by the opposing party.

questions.def: 'Are required' shows passive voice: applicants are acted upon.
questions.question: All applicants ___ to submit their transcripts.

questions.def: 'Will be' is used to form the future passive.
questions.question: The truth ___ eventually revealed.

questions.def: 'Were' is the correct plural past passive form.
questions.question: The changes ___ thoroughly discussed at the meeting.

questions.def: Passive voice: 'was' + past participle to describe a completed action.
questions.question: The new policy ___ by the board last week.

questions.def: 'Should be reviewed' is passive, indicating necessity of review.
questions.question: The documents ___ before being filed.

questions.def: 'Being done' is the correct passive construction for continuous tense.
questions.question: The mistake was being doing during the audit.

questions.def: 'Be informed' is the passive infinitive after 'expect'.
questions.question: I expect to ___ of the decision soon.

questions.def: 'Were communicated' is the correct passive form for past tense.
questions.question: The results ___ to the research team.

questions.def: 'Are easily made' is the correct passive construction with an adverb.
questions.question: Mistakes ___ if attention is not paid.

questions.def: Correct passive infinitive is 'to have escaped', not 'to be escaping'.
questions.question: The suspect is believed to be escaping.
